memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out of it." - Exodus 7:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh had sneered, who is the Lord? Now God answers: the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.

This is worth pausing over. The plagues were not merely about getting Israel out. They were also about making God known to Egypt. Even in judgement, God was revealing Himself to a nation that did not worship Him.

Egypt worshipped the Nile, the sun, frogs, cattle, and Pharaoh himself. One by one, God would show that each of these so-called powers was nothing before Him. It was a public dismantling of false gods.

And remarkably, some Egyptians did respond. By the time Israel left, a mixed multitude went with them, and later some Egyptian servants believed God's warnings and sheltered their livestock.

God's heart has never been for one nation only. Even here, in a book about Israel's rescue, He is making Himself known to outsiders. That thread runs all the way to the promise that people from every nation will stand before the throne (Rev 7:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What false securities in my life need to be exposed as powerless?
2. Do I believe God desires to be known by people far outside my circle?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make Yourself known — in my life, and among people who do not yet know You. Tear down whatever I have wrongly trusted. Amen.
